title: Swiggy Taps Former Myntra CEO Nandita Sinha to Lead Instamart
excerpt: Sinha will take charge of Swiggy's quick commerce arm on August 3, replacing outgoing CEO Amitesh Jha as competition in India's $11.5 billion rapid-delivery market intensifies.
body:
• Swiggy has appointed former Myntra CEO Nandita Sinha as the new chief executive of Instamart, effective August 3
  • She succeeds Amitesh Kumar Jha, who led Instamart through a major expansion phase and improved its contribution margins
  • Sinha brings over 20 years of experience across Myntra, Flipkart, Britannia and Hindustan Unilever
  • The appointment comes as India's quick commerce sector — valued at $11.5 billion — faces mounting competition from Amazon and Flipkart

New Leadership at Instamart

Swiggy on Tuesday named Nandita Sinha, the former chief executive of fashion e-commerce platform Myntra, as the new CEO of its quick commerce business Instamart, according to Reuters. The appointment takes effect on August 3.

Sinha replaces Amitesh Kumar Jha, who has resigned after steering the platform through a critical growth period. Swiggy Managing Director and Group CEO Sriharsha Majety confirmed both moves in a company statement.

"Nandita is one of India's most accomplished consumer internet leaders, and I'm enthusiastic about the vision, customer obsession and operational rigour she brings to the team we've built at Instamart."

— Sriharsha Majety, MD & Group CEO, Swiggy

A Seasoned E-Commerce Veteran

Sinha brings more than two decades of leadership experience spanning e-commerce, retail and fast-moving consumer goods. At Myntra, she oversaw consistent growth and strengthened the platform's market positioning, according to Analytics Insight. Before that, she held senior roles at Flipkart, Britannia Industries and Hindustan Unilever — a career arc that gave her deep exposure to digital commerce, branding and consumer-facing business at scale.

Her mandate at Instamart will centre on assortment expansion, customer experience improvements and operational execution, according to Outlook Business. The hire signals Swiggy's intent to bring a consumer-retail mindset to its rapid-delivery operation as the segment evolves beyond groceries into multiple retail categories.

Jha's Legacy and Exit

Majety acknowledged Amitesh Jha's contributions during his tenure, crediting him with scaling Instamart through a pivotal growth phase and building what the company called a "strong, high-performing culture." Jha, a chemical engineering graduate from IIT Delhi with an MBA from IIM Ahmedabad, joined Swiggy from Flipkart in 2024 and played a key role in improving Instamart's contribution margins and strengthening its differentiation strategy, including initiatives such as Noice.

"Over his tenure, he has been instrumental in scaling Instamart through a critical growth phase, building a strong, high-performing culture, and leaving the organisation in a solid, well-run state."

— Sriharsha Majety on Amitesh Jha's departure

A Crowded Battlefield

The leadership transition arrives at a turbulent moment for India's quick commerce market, currently estimated at $11.5 billion, according to Indian Retailer. Investors have raised concerns about slowing growth at Instamart even as rivals ramp up spending on dark stores, logistics infrastructure and delivery capabilities.

Amazon and Walmart-owned Flipkart have both accelerated their quick commerce rollouts in India, increasingly targeting smaller cities to compete with domestic players for market share. The push has turned rapid delivery from a metro convenience into a nationwide land grab, with operators racing to lock in customers across groceries, electronics and fashion.

For Swiggy — which listed on the NSE last year under the ticker SWIG.NS — the Instamart business is a critical growth engine alongside its core food delivery operation. Installing a proven e-commerce executive like Sinha at the helm reflects the company's recognition that quick commerce now demands the same retail sophistication as traditional online shopping.

What's Next

Sinha's immediate priorities will likely include defending Instamart's position against well-funded competitors while expanding the platform's product range and geographic footprint. Her experience navigating Myntra's competitive fashion e-commerce market could prove valuable as quick commerce platforms increasingly compete on selection and brand partnerships rather than delivery speed alone.

The appointment also raises questions about whether Swiggy will pursue further structural changes to its leadership or business strategy as the quick commerce race enters its next phase. With Amazon, Flipkart and established players like Zepto and Blinkit all vying for dominance, the margin for error is thin.
